headline: Youth detained over 'sniper' comment on PM's bus
summary: Abu Bokor Siddique was picked up by detectives in Rajshahi after posting a Facebook comment suggesting a sniper could have targeted the Prime Minister's vehicle.
details: Detectives have detained a young man from Rajshahi after he posted a Facebook comment suggesting a sniper could have targeted a university bus carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
The suspect, identified as Abu Bokor Siddique, was picked up by a team from the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s (DMP) Detective Branch and DMP's Special Response Battalion (SRB).
The incident stems from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to Rajshahi on Tuesday, where he traveled in a RUET university bus instead of his usual bulletproof vehicle.
A Facebook page called “The Beauty of Rajshahi” had posted about the bus, to which Abu Bokor Siddique commented: “What a golden chance. All that was missing was a sniper.”
Md Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner (DB) of DMP, described the comment as an 'outrageous threat' to the prime minister's security.
The suspect is being brought to Dhaka for further questioning by the Detective Branch.
Deputy Commissioner Gaziur Rahman of the Rajshahi Metropolitan Police had previously confirmed that the commenter had been identified and legal action was under way.

headline: Army exchanges fire with armed group in Sajek after blockade
summary: Over 2,300 tourists were stranded as the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF) blockaded the area and opened fire on law enforcers.
details: The Bangladesh Army exchanged fire with an armed group in Rangamati’s tourist spot Sajek on Thursday. The clash occurred after two local organisations blockaded the area, leaving over 2,300 tourists stranded on their way back.

The shooting began around 11:30 am near Ujo Bazar. According to Sajek Police chief Toffazzal Hossain, the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF) opened fire at law enforcers, prompting the army to return fire.
A spokesperson for the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Directorate confirmed the exchange of fire, stating it was necessary to bring the situation under control.
Once the situation calmed, law enforcement agencies safely escorted the stranded tourists out of Sajek. The situation returned to normal about an hour after the initial clash.
caption:
